text:
The fluorescent hum of Aisle 4 felt strangely like a classroom silence. Mr. Henderson, now stooped and leaning heavily on his cane, reached for a tin of peaches just as a hand brushed his elbow. He flinched, then looked up into the wide, familiar eyes of Sarah Jenkins.

Twenty years had carved new lines into her face, but that same spark of curiosity remained. She froze, holding a box of cereal like a shield. "Mr. H?" she whispered, the title slipping out instinctively.

He blinked, the fog of retirement lifting momentarily. "Sarah. You were... you were always asking about the stars."

"I still do," she smiled, a nervous twitch in her lips. "Though I don’t look through telescopes anymore. I just buy them in the hardware store."

They stood there, two ghosts from different timelines colliding in the mundane reality of grocery shopping. The awkwardness hung thick, heavier than the canned goods surrounding them. Finally, he patted her arm gently. "You did good, Sarah. I heard you became an architect."

She nodded, tears pricking her eyes. "And you retired, Mr. H. Did you ever finish that book?"

He shook his head, smiling sadly. "No. But I met my best student in aisle four. That’s enough."
